preamble: Devoicing of the alveolar implosive to [t]. In Katuic, the Chatong dialect of Ngeq has t with a breathy vowel where Ngeq (Kriang) and Katu keep d or ɗ: Proto-Katuic *ɗak 'trap' > ta̤k, *ɗaak 'water' > ta̤ak, *ɗoom 'ripe' > to̤om (Sidwell 2005). Chatong devoices the plain voiced stops in the same way (*dal 'prop up' > ta̤l, *kduŋ 'bag' > katṳŋ), but no source records or reconstructs a stage with d for Chatong. The Pearic languages also have t for Proto-Austroasiatic *ɗ: *ɗakʔ 'trap' > Chong ta̤k (Bahnar đăk keeps the implosive), *ɗaːkʔ 'water' > Chong ta̤ːk, Pear téâk. The breathy vowel of Chong continues a former voiced onset, as in Chong plṳː 'thigh' < Proto-Pearic *bluː, and Headley (1985) reconstructs Proto-Pearic *daːk 'water' with plain *d, so Pearic is filed in two steps, under ɗ > d and d > t. Khmer reached t in two attested steps: Proto-Austroasiatic *ɗaːkʔ 'water' > Old Khmer ទិក៑ dik > Modern Khmer ទឹក /tɨk/, filed under ɗ > d and d > t. Modern Khmer ɗ (ដ) is secondary, from earlier *t (ដៃ 'hand' < Proto-Mon-Khmer *t₁iiʔ).
